passages.title: The Honeybee Dance
passages.text: Honeybees live together in large groups called colonies. When a bee finds a good source of food, such as a field of flowers, it returns to the hive and shares the news with the other bees. It does this by moving in a special pattern that scientists call a "waggle dance." The direction of the dance tells the other bees which way to fly, and the length of the dance tells them how far away the food is. This simple system allows thousands of bees to work together without speaking. Because of the waggle dance, a single hive can collect food from a very wide area. Scientists find the dance fascinating because it shows that even small animals can share detailed information in a clear and useful way.

questions.p: What is the main topic of the passage?
o: How honeybees tell each other where to find food.
How scientists keep bees as pets.
questions.e: הקטע כולו עוסק באופן שבו דבורים מודיעות זו לזו היכן נמצא מזון באמצעות "ריקוד הנדנוד".

questions.p: According to the passage, what does the direction of the dance tell other bees?
o: How many flowers are in the field.
How long the food will last.
Which way they should fly to reach the food.
questions.e: בקטע נכתב במפורש: "The direction of the dance tells the other bees which way to fly".

questions.p: The length of the dance shows the other bees:
o: how far away the food is.
questions.e: נכתב: "the length of the dance tells them how far away the food is".

questions.p: What does the word "colonies" mean in the passage?
o: Large groups of bees living together.
Long flights made by single bees.
questions.e: המשפט הראשון מסביר: "large groups called colonies", כלומר קבוצות גדולות של דבורים.

questions.p: Why can a single hive collect food from a wide area?
o: Because each bee flies alone without help.
Because the hive moves from place to place.
Because flowers grow only near the hive.
Because the dance lets many bees share useful information.
questions.e: הקטע מקשר בין הריקוד המשותף ליכולת לאסוף מזון משטח רחב: "Because of the waggle dance, a single hive can collect food from a very wide area".

passages.title: Reading on Paper or on Screen
passages.text: Today, students can read their books either on paper or on a screen. Both choices have their advantages. Paper books are easy on the eyes and do not need electricity, so they can be read anywhere. Screens, on the other hand, can hold hundreds of books in one small device and let readers change the size of the letters. Some studies suggest that people remember information better when they read it on paper, especially for difficult subjects. However, screens are very useful for quick reading and for searching inside a text. Many teachers now tell their students to use both. For careful study, they suggest paper, and for fast reading or research, they suggest a screen. In this way, students can enjoy the benefits of each.

o: Why screens are always better than paper.
How to build a reading device.
Why students should stop reading books.
The advantages of reading on paper and on screens.
questions.e: הקטע משווה את היתרונות של קריאה על נייר ועל מסך, ולכן זהו הנושא המרכזי.

o: let readers change the letter size.
are useful for searching inside a text.
questions.e: נכתב: "Paper books are easy on the eyes and do not need electricity".

questions.p: What is one advantage of screens mentioned in the passage?

They are easier on the eyes than paper.
questions.e: נכתב: "Screens ... can hold hundreds of books in one small device".

questions.p: What do some studies suggest about reading on paper?

Paper is always cheaper than screens.
People may remember difficult information better.
Paper books are harder to carry.
questions.e: נכתב: "people remember information better when they read it on paper, especially for difficult subjects".

questions.p: For fast reading and research, the passage suggests using:

passages.text: Long ago, most gardens belonged to kings and rich families, and ordinary people were not allowed to enter them. As cities grew larger and more crowded, leaders began to worry about the health of city workers. They noticed that people who lived far from green spaces were often tired and sick. To solve this problem, some cities opened the first public parks, which anyone could visit for free. These parks gave families a place to rest, walk, and breathe fresh air. Children could play outside safely, away from busy streets. Over time, public parks became a normal part of city life. Today, almost every large city has parks, and many people see them as one of the most valuable parts of their neighborhood.

passages.title: Why We Yawn
passages.text: Almost everyone yawns, yet for a long time no one was sure why. A yawn is a deep breath in which the mouth opens wide and air fills the lungs. People often yawn when they are tired or bored, but they also yawn at other times. One popular idea is that yawning helps cool the brain. When the brain becomes a little too warm, a yawn brings in cool air and may help it work better. Another interesting fact is that yawning seems to spread from person to person. If one person in a room yawns, others often yawn soon after, even if they are not tired. Scientists believe this "catching" of yawns may be linked to the way humans copy one another. Although we still do not have all the answers, yawning remains a small but curious part of being human.

passages.title: The Story of Chocolate
passages.text: Chocolate comes from the seeds of the cacao tree, which grows in warm places near the equator. Hundreds of years ago, people in Central America were the first to use these seeds. They did not eat sweet chocolate bars as we do today. Instead, they made a bitter drink by mixing ground cacao with water and spices. This drink was so valued that the seeds were sometimes used as money. When the drink later reached Europe, people there added sugar and milk to make it sweeter. Over time, factories learned to turn chocolate into the solid bars that are now sold around the world. Today, chocolate is one of the most popular treats on the planet, but few people know that it began as a bitter drink far from the candy shops of today.

passages.title: The Hidden Network of Trees
passages.text: For a long time, people thought of a forest as a simple collection of separate trees competing for sunlight. Recent research, however, suggests a more surprising picture. Beneath the soil, the roots of many trees are connected by a vast web of tiny fungthreads called mycelium. Through this underground network, trees can share water, nutrients, and even chemical signals. A large, healthy tree may send extra sugar to a smaller, shaded neighbor that cannot make enough food on its own. When one tree is attacked by insects, it can release signals that warn nearby trees, giving them time to strengthen their defenses. Some scientists now describe a forest less as a group of rivals and more as a cooperative community. This view does not mean that competition disappears, but it shows that survival in a forest depends on connection as much as on strength.

Sunlight is the only thing trees need to survive.
questions.e: הקטע מציג תמונה חדשה: עצים מחוברים ומשתפים פעולה, ולא רק מתחרים.

questions.p: What connects the roots of many trees beneath the soil?

questions.e: נכתב: "the roots of many trees are connected by a vast web of tiny fungthreads called mycelium".

o: Send it extra sugar when it cannot make enough food.

questions.e: נכתב: "A large, healthy tree may send extra sugar to a smaller, shaded neighbor".

As a collection of identical trees.
As a cooperative community rather than only a group of rivals.
questions.e: נכתב: "Some scientists now describe a forest less as a group of rivals and more as a cooperative community".

passages.title: The Limits of Multitasking
passages.text: Many people believe they can do several demanding tasks at once, such as writing an essay while replying to messages. Psychologists, however, have found that the human brain does not truly perform two difficult tasks at the same time. Instead, it switches rapidly between them. Each switch takes a small amount of time and mental effort, and these costs add up. As a result, people who try to multitask often work more slowly and make more mistakes than those who focus on one task at a time. The feeling of being productive can be misleading, because constant switching keeps the mind busy without improving the quality of the work. Researchers suggest that grouping similar tasks together and limiting interruptions can lead to better results. Far from being a sign of a sharp mind, heavy multitasking may actually reduce both speed and accuracy.

questions.p: What is the main point of the passage?
o: The brain easily handles many hard tasks at once.
Replying to messages is the most important task.
People should never work on essays.
Multitasking usually lowers speed and accuracy rather than raising them.
questions.e: הרעיון המרכזי: ריבוי משימות בדרך כלל מפחית מהירות ודיוק במקום לשפר אותם.

o: It performs two hard tasks at exactly the same time.
It stops working on both tasks.
It remembers tasks but does not do them.
questions.e: נכתב: "Instead, it switches rapidly between them".

questions.p: Why do the costs of switching matter?
o: Switching makes tasks easier each time.
Each switch takes time and effort, and these costs add up.
Switching uses no mental effort at all.
Switching only affects very simple tasks.
questions.e: נכתב: "Each switch takes a small amount of time and mental effort, and these costs add up".

o: Constant switching keeps the mind busy without improving the work.

Switching always improves the quality of work.
questions.e: נכתב: "constant switching keeps the mind busy without improving the quality of the work".

Group similar tasks together and limit interruptions.
Always work on the hardest tasks together.
questions.e: נכתב: "grouping similar tasks together and limiting interruptions can lead to better results".

passages.text: When the bicycle first became popular in the late nineteenth century, it changed daily life in ways that few people had expected. Before the bicycle, most ordinary people could travel only as far as they could walk, unless they could afford a horse. The bicycle offered a cheap and reliable way to cover longer distances. Workers could live farther from their jobs, and young people could visit friends in nearby towns. The bicycle also played a surprising role in social change. For many women, it provided a new sense of freedom and independence, since they could now travel on their own. Clothing styles even began to change to make riding easier. Although cars later became the main form of transport, the bicycle had already shown how a simple machine could widen the world of the ordinary person.

passages.title: Why Coral Reefs Matter
passages.text: Coral reefs cover only a tiny fraction of the ocean floor, yet they support an enormous share of all sea life. These reefs are built by small animals called corals, which slowly create hard structures over many years. The complex shapes of a reef provide shelter and food for countless fish and other creatures. In this way, a healthy reef acts like an underwater city, full of activity. Reefs also protect coastlines by breaking the force of large waves before they reach the shore. However, coral reefs are very sensitive to changes in their environment. When the water becomes too warm, corals can lose their color and, if the heat continues, may die. Pollution and overfishing add further pressure. Because so many species and communities depend on them, protecting coral reefs has become an important goal for scientists and governments alike.

passages.title: The Science of Sleep
passages.text: Sleep may look like a time when the body does nothing, but in fact a great deal happens during these hours. While we sleep, the brain sorts through the events of the day and strengthens the memories worth keeping. The body also repairs tissues, builds energy, and supports the systems that fight illness. People who regularly sleep too little often struggle to concentrate and may become more easily upset. Over many years, poor sleep has been linked to a range of health problems. Despite this, many adults treat sleep as something they can cut whenever they are busy. Researchers warn that this is a mistake. Although the right amount of sleep varies from person to person, most adults need around seven to eight hours each night. Rather than a waste of time, sleep is one of the most active and useful parts of a healthy life.

passages.title: The Paradox of Choice
passages.text: It is widely assumed that more choice is always better, yet research in psychology has complicated this belief. When people face only a handful of options, they tend to choose with relative ease and to feel satisfied afterward. As the number of options grows, however, the decision can become harder rather than simpler. With too many alternatives, individuals may struggle to compare them, delay their decision, or avoid choosing altogether. Even after they decide, they are more likely to wonder whether a different option would have been better, which can reduce their satisfaction. This does not imply that choice is undesirable; a reasonable range of options allows people to find what suits them. The point, rather, is that the relationship between choice and happiness is not straightforward. Beyond a certain threshold, additional options may impose a hidden cost in the form of doubt and regret.

questions.e: נכתב: "the decision can become harder rather than simpler".

questions.e: נכתב: "they are more likely to wonder whether a different option would have been better, which can reduce their satisfaction".

questions.e: נכתב: "a reasonable range of options allows people to find what suits them".

passages.title: The Replication Problem in Science
passages.text: A central principle of science is that a genuine result should be repeatable: if an experiment is conducted again under the same conditions, it ought to produce a similar outcome. In recent years, however, researchers in several fields have discovered that a worrying number of published findings cannot be reproduced. There are many possible reasons. Some studies rely on small samples, which can produce results that appear meaningful but arise largely by chance. Others may be influenced, perhaps unintentionally, by the expectations of the researchers themselves. There is also pressure to publish striking results, which can discourage scientists from reporting experiments that failed. None of this means that science is broken. On the contrary, the very fact that the problem has been identified reflects the self-correcting nature of the scientific process. By demanding stronger methods and greater openness, the scientific community is working to ensure that published claims rest on firmer ground.

questions.e: הרעיון המרכזי: ממצאים רבים אינם ניתנים לשחזור, אך המדע מתקן את הבעיה.

questions.e: נכתב: "a genuine result should be repeatable: if an experiment is conducted again under the same conditions, it ought to produce a similar outcome".

questions.e: נכתב: "pressure to publish striking results ... can discourage scientists from reporting experiments that failed".

passages.title: Language and Color
passages.text: The colors of the rainbow appear to be a fixed feature of the physical world, yet the way languages divide them varies considerably. Some languages use only two or three basic color terms, grouping together shades that English speakers would treat as distinct. Others draw finer distinctions, with separate words for hues that English lumps under a single label. Researchers have asked whether these differences shape how people actually perceive color. The evidence is mixed. People can usually see and distinguish far more colors than their language names, which suggests that perception is not strictly limited by vocabulary. At the same time, studies indicate that speakers may sort and remember colors slightly faster when their language provides a ready word for them. The debate illustrates a broader question in the study of language: whether the words available to us merely describe our thoughts or also, in subtle ways, help to shape them.

passages.title: The Tragedy of the Commons
passages.text: Imagine a shared pasture open to all the herders of a village. Each herder gains directly by adding one more animal to the land, since the profit from that animal is entirely his own. The cost of overgrazing, however, is shared by everyone. Because the individual benefit is concentrated while the harm is spread thin, every herder has an incentive to add more animals, even though the combined effect ruins the pasture for all. This pattern, often called the tragedy of the commons, appears wherever a valuable resource is shared but unregulated, from fisheries to clean air. The example is not an argument against cooperation but a warning about how rational individual choices can lead to a collectively poor outcome. Solutions usually involve agreed rules, shared responsibility, or limits on use, which align private incentives with the long-term health of the resource.

passages.title: The Placebo Effect
passages.text: When a patient is given a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill, they sometimes report a genuine improvement in how they feel. This phenomenon, known as the placebo effect, has long puzzled and intrigued researchers. It demonstrates that a person’s expectations can influence their physical experience, particularly for symptoms such as pain, fatigue, or low mood. The effect appears strongest when patients believe in the treatment and trust the person providing it. Importantly, the placebo effect does not mean that symptoms are imaginary; rather, it reveals how closely the mind and body are linked. For medical research, the effect poses a challenge. To judge whether a new drug truly works, scientists must compare it against a placebo, ensuring that any benefit goes beyond what expectation alone could produce. In this way, an effect once dismissed as a nuisance has become an essential tool in testing modern medicine.

To avoid testing the drug on patients.
To prove that the drug has no effect.
questions.e: נכתב: "scientists must compare it against a placebo, ensuring that any benefit goes beyond what expectation alone could produce".

passages.title: The Limits of Eyewitness Testimony
passages.text: Eyewitness testimony has traditionally been regarded as among the most persuasive forms of evidence, on the assumption that memory preserves experience much as a recording preserves sound. Decades of research have undermined this assumption. Memory, it turns out, is not a faithful archive but a reconstructive process: each act of recollection rebuilds an event from fragments, and in doing so is vulnerable to distortion. Subtle features of how a question is posed can reshape what a witness later "remembers," and confident testimony is not necessarily accurate testimony. The implications are significant, since jurors tend to place great weight on a witness who speaks with conviction. None of this renders eyewitness accounts worthless; they remain valuable when corroborated and gathered carefully. The lesson is more measured: such testimony must be treated as evidence to be weighed rather than as an unquestionable record, and legal systems have begun, slowly, to adjust their procedures accordingly.

questions.p: What is the central claim of the passage?
o: Eyewitness testimony is the most reliable form of evidence.
Eyewitness memory is reconstructive and can be distorted, so testimony must be weighed carefully.
Memory works exactly like a sound recording.
Eyewitness accounts are worthless and should be ignored.
questions.e: הטענה המרכזית: הזיכרון משחזר ועלול להיות מעוות, ולכן יש לשקול עדות בזהירות.

o: That witnesses always lie in court.
That memory cannot be tested at all.
That memory preserves experience like a recording.
questions.e: נכתב: "memory preserves experience much as a recording preserves sound", הנחה שהמחקר ערער.

As a reconstructive process that rebuilds events from fragments.
As a process that never changes.
As a recording that cannot be edited.
questions.e: נכתב: "Memory ... is not a faithful archive but a reconstructive process: each act of recollection rebuilds an event from fragments".

questions.e: נכתב: "confident testimony is not necessarily accurate testimony".

Jurors tend to place great weight on a confident witness.
Jurors are not allowed to hear testimony.
questions.e: נכתב: "jurors tend to place great weight on a witness who speaks with conviction".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The two terms are often used ____, though they mean different things.
questions.e: Interchangeably = כבני חלופה. "though they mean different things" מצביע על שימוש שגוי כבני חלופה.

questions.p: The plan was praised in principle but ____ in its details.
questions.e: הניגוד "praised in principle but" מחייב פועל שלילי: questioned (הוטל בו ספק).

questions.p: The experiment’s design was ____, allowing few alternative explanations.
questions.e: Robust = איתן/חזק. תכנון שמותיר מעט הסברים חלופיים הוא איתן.

questions.p: The argument is ____, mistaking correlation for causation.
questions.e: Flawed = פגום. בלבול בין מתאם לסיבתיות הופך טיעון לפגום.

questions.p: His reasoning is ____, each step following necessarily from the last.
questions.e: Rigorous = קפדני/הדוק. צעדים הנובעים בהכרח זה מזה מאפיינים חשיבה הדוקה.

questions.p: The theory has ____ implications that reach far beyond its field.
questions.e: Far-reaching = מרחיקות לכת. השלכות שחורגות הרבה מעבר לתחום הן מרחיקות לכת.

sections.descHe: קראו את הקטע האקדמי הקצר ולאחר מכן ענו על השאלות הנוגעות אליו. כל התשובות מתבססות על המידע שבטקסט בלבד.

questions.p: What paradox does the passage describe?
o: Standards are useless and should be abolished.
Standards always improve over time automatically.
Standardization is essential yet can lock in early choices and limit alternatives.
Standardization has no effect on trade or cost.
questions.e: הפרדוקס: הסטנדרטיזציה הכרחית אך עלולה לקבע בחירות מוקדמות ולצמצם חלופות.

questions.p: How does standardization help complex systems, according to the passage?
o: It prevents any trade between regions.
It makes all products more expensive.
It ensures that components made in different places fit together.
questions.e: נכתב: "By ensuring that components made in different places fit together, standardization lowers costs, enables trade".

questions.p: Why does switching to a superior alternative become difficult?
o: A standard’s value lies largely in how many others use it.
No one ever wants a better design.
Standards have no users at all.
questions.e: נכתב: "the value of a standard lies largely in how many others use it".

questions.p: Why might a technically inferior design persist?
o: Because it is always the cheapest option.
Because it arrived first and accumulated users.
Because it has no users at all.
questions.e: נכתב: "A technically inferior design may therefore persist simply because it arrived first and accumulated users".

questions.p: What additional concern do critics raise?
o: Standards treat every group exactly the same.
Standards encode assumptions that may suit some groups better than others.
Standards remove all assumptions from design.
questions.e: נכתב: "standards encode particular assumptions and priorities, which may suit some groups better than others".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט מקור באנגלית. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המשפט הקרוב ביותר במשמעותו למשפט המקורי, גם אם הניסוח שונה.

questions.p: The novel subverts the very conventions it appears to embrace.
o: The novel faithfully upholds the conventions it follows.
The novel undermines the very traditions it seems to follow.
The novel openly rejects all literary conventions.
The novel ignores conventions it neither follows nor breaks.
questions.e: "subverts the very conventions it appears to embrace" = חותרת תחת אותן מוסכמות שלכאורה היא מאמצת. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על הניגוד הפנימי.

questions.p: His argument hinges on a premise that many scholars find untenable.
o: His argument stands firm regardless of its premise.
Most scholars accept the premise of his argument.
His whole argument depends on an assumption that many scholars reject as indefensible.
His argument depends on a premise everyone agrees with.
questions.e: "hinges on a premise ... untenable" = תלוי בהנחה שרבים רואים כבלתי ניתנת להגנה. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על התלות ועל הדחייה.

questions.p: The reforms, while well-intentioned, inadvertently widened existing inequalities.
o: Although the reforms meant well, they accidentally made existing gaps larger.
The reforms deliberately reduced existing inequalities.
The well-meant reforms had no effect on inequalities.
The reforms intentionally widened the inequalities.
questions.e: "well-intentioned ... inadvertently widened ... inequalities" = בכוונה טובה, אך הרחיבו בלי כוונה את הפערים. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "meant well ... accidentally made existing gaps larger".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט מקור באנגלית. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המשפט הקרוב ביותר במשמעותו למשפט המקורי, גם אם הניסוח שונה.

questions.p: Such an interpretation, plausible as it may seem, overlooks crucial historical context.
o: However reasonable that reading looks, it ignores essential historical background.
That interpretation carefully accounts for all historical context.
The interpretation is implausible and based only on history.
Historical context makes that interpretation impossible to hold.
questions.e: "plausible as it may seem, overlooks crucial historical context" = סבירה ככל שתיראה, מתעלמת מהקשר היסטורי מהותי. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על הוויתור ועל ההתעלמות.

questions.p: The data lend credence to the claim that early intervention is decisive.
o: The data cast serious doubt on the value of early intervention.
The data make the claim that early intervention is crucial more believable.
The data prove that early intervention makes no difference.
The data suggest that late intervention is what matters.
questions.e: "lend credence to the claim" = מחזקות את הטענה. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "make the claim ... more believable".

questions.p: Only by questioning long-standing assumptions can genuine progress be achieved.
o: Progress comes only from accepting long-standing assumptions.
Questioning old assumptions prevents any genuine progress.
Genuine progress requires ignoring all assumptions entirely.
Real progress is possible just when we challenge assumptions held for a long time.
questions.e: "Only by questioning ... can genuine progress be achieved" = רק ערעור על הנחות ותיקות מאפשר התקדמות. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על התנאי ההכרחי.

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The report ____ the issue, offering little in the way of solutions.
questions.e: Oversimplify = לפשט יתר על המידה. ראיה שטחית של בעיה מובילה למעט פתרונות.

questions.p: The new evidence ____ doubt on the established explanation.
questions.e: Cast doubt on = להטיל ספק ב. הראיות החדשות מטילות ספק בהסבר המקובל.

questions.p: The author writes with ____, never wasting a single word.
questions.e: Economy (of language) = חסכנות לשונית. "never wasting a word" מגדיר זאת.

questions.p: The reform was ____ by political infighting before it could take effect.
questions.e: Derail = להכשיל/להוציא מהמסלול. מאבקים פוליטיים הכשילו את הרפורמה.

questions.p: The painting’s power is ____, resisting any single interpretation.
questions.e: Elusive = חמקמק. כוח שמתחמק מפרשנות אחת הוא חמקמק.

questions.p: The witness’s story, ____ plausible, lacked corroborating evidence.
questions.e: While כאן = אף ש. ניגוד בין סבירות הסיפור לבין היעדר תימוכין.

title: סימולציה 18 — קשה
description: סימולציה מאתגרת בשישה פרקי הליבה של האמירנט, ברמה גבוהה ומיועדת למי שמכוון לציון גבוה.

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The company plans to ____ its services to new markets.
questions.e: Expand = להרחיב. החברה מתכננת להרחיב שירותים לשווקים חדשים.

questions.p: The reform was ____ because it failed to consider local conditions.
questions.e: Ineffective = בלתי יעיל. התעלמות מתנאים מקומיים הופכת רפורמה לבלתי יעילה.

questions.p: The witness recounted the events with remarkable ____.
questions.e: Accuracy = דיוק. "recounted the events" מתאים לתיאור מדויק.

questions.p: The reform’s success ____ on factors outside the planners’ control.
questions.e: Depend on = להיות תלוי ב. ההצלחה הייתה תלויה בגורמים חיצוניים.

questions.p: His critique is ____, dismantling the theory point by point.
questions.e: Devastating = הרסני/מוחץ. פירוק התאוריה נקודה אחר נקודה מצביע על ביקורת מוחצת.

questions.p: The findings ____ a more cautious interpretation than the authors offer.
questions.e: Warrant = להצדיק/לחייב. הממצאים מצדיקים פרשנות זהירה יותר.

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The committee’s recommendation was ____ ignored by the management.
questions.e: Largely = במידה רבה. ההנהלה התעלמה במידה רבה מההמלצה.

questions.p: The conclusion is ____, since the premises do not actually support it.
questions.e: Unwarranted = בלתי מוצדק. אם ההנחות אינן תומכות, המסקנה אינה מוצדקת.

questions.p: The argument relies on a ____ that the two cases are truly comparable.
questions.e: Assumption = הנחה. הטיעון מסתמך על ההנחה שהמקרים דומים.

questions.p: The lecture ____ a subject that most prefer to avoid.
questions.e: Confront = להתמודד עם. הניגוד מול "prefer to avoid" מחייב פועל של התמודדות.

questions.p: The reform was ____ in name only, leaving the system untouched.
questions.e: "revolutionary in name only", מהפכנית בשם בלבד. הניגוד מול "untouched" מחייב מילה גדולה.

questions.p: The reform ____ a delicate balance between competing interests.
questions.e: Strike a balance = ליצור איזון. הרפורמה יוצרת איזון עדין בין אינטרסים מתחרים.

sections.descHe: קראו את הקטע האקדמי הקצר ולאחר מכן ענו על השאלות הנוגעות אליו. כל התשובות מתבססות על המידע שבטקסט בלבד.

questions.p: What is the main argument of the passage?
o: Predictive algorithms are perfectly objective and fair.
Predictive algorithms should be banned entirely.
Human judgment is always better than any algorithm.
Predictive algorithms can reproduce past bias and must be scrutinized, not blindly trusted.
questions.e: הטיעון המרכזי: אלגוריתמים חזויים עלולים לשכפל הטיות מהעבר ויש לבחון אותם, לא לבטוח בהם בעיניים עצומות.

questions.p: What is the stated appeal of predictive algorithms?
o: They promise faster, seemingly more objective decisions than humans.
They remove the need for any data.
They guarantee that no mistakes occur.
They make all human workers unnecessary.
questions.e: נכתב: "they promise to replace inconsistent human judgment with something faster and ostensibly more objective".

questions.p: Why is true objectivity hard for these algorithms to achieve?
o: They are never trained on any data.
They are designed to be unfair on purpose.
They absorb the patterns in historical data, including past discrimination.
questions.e: נכתב: "An algorithm trained on historical data inevitably absorbs the patterns embedded in that data, including patterns that reflect past discrimination".

questions.p: What problem does the opacity of these systems cause?
o: It makes the systems run more slowly.
It removes all bias from the systems.
It is hard for affected people to understand or contest decisions.
It allows everyone to see the data clearly.
questions.e: נכתב: "many such systems are opaque, making it hard for those affected to understand or contest the decisions".

questions.p: What does the author propose as the proper response?
o: Subjecting the tools to scrutiny, auditing, and transparency.
Hiding the outcomes from the public.
questions.e: נכתב: "The proper response is not to abandon these tools ... but to subject them to scrutiny: auditing their outcomes, demanding transparency".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט מקור באנגלית. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המשפט הקרוב ביותר במשמעותו למשפט המקורי, גם אם הניסוח שונה.

questions.p: The witness’s account, corroborated by physical evidence, proved compelling.
o: The witness’s account was rejected for lacking any evidence.
Physical evidence contradicted the witness’s account.
The witness’s account was convincing despite the missing evidence.
Backed up by physical evidence, the witness’s account turned out to be convincing.
questions.e: Corroborate = לאשש; compelling = משכנע. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "backed up by physical evidence ... convincing".

questions.p: The policy’s benefits, considerable though they are, do not justify its costs.
o: Although the policy brings substantial benefits, they are not worth what it costs.
The policy’s small benefits easily justify its costs.
The policy’s benefits clearly outweigh its costs.
The policy has no benefits and only heavy costs.
questions.e: "considerable though they are, do not justify its costs" = ניכרות ככל שיהיו, אינן מצדיקות את העלות. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על הוויתור ועל המסקנה.

questions.p: Critics contend that the model oversimplifies a fundamentally complex phenomenon.
o: Critics agree the model captures all the phenomenon’s complexity.
Critics maintain that the model treats a deeply complex phenomenon too simply.
Critics say the model makes a simple phenomenon too complicated.
Critics ignore how the model handles the phenomenon.
questions.e: Contend = לטעון; oversimplify = לפשט יתר על המידה. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "treats a deeply complex phenomenon too simply".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט מקור באנגלית. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המשפט הקרוב ביותר במשמעותו למשפט המקורי, גם אם הניסוח שונה.

questions.p: Notwithstanding its initial appeal, the scheme soon revealed serious shortcomings.
o: Because it looked attractive, the scheme proved flawless.
The scheme had no appeal and no shortcomings.
The scheme’s weaknesses appeared before it was launched.
In spite of how attractive it looked at first, the scheme quickly showed major weaknesses.
questions.e: Notwithstanding = על אף; shortcomings = ליקויים. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "in spite of how attractive it looked ... showed major weaknesses".

questions.p: The findings underscore the extent to which environment shapes behaviour.
o: The findings show that environment has little effect on behaviour.
The findings prove that behaviour shapes the environment.
The findings highlight just how much the surroundings influence behaviour.
The findings ignore the link between environment and behaviour.
questions.e: "underscore the extent to which environment shapes behaviour" = מדגישות עד כמה הסביבה מעצבת התנהגות. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על המשמעות והכיוון.

questions.p: The proposal was met with skepticism, if not outright hostility.
o: The proposal was welcomed with great enthusiasm.
The proposal was received with doubt, and at times even open hostility.
The proposal was accepted without any doubt at all.
The proposal was met with friendliness rather than doubt.
questions.e: "skepticism, if not outright hostility" = ספקנות, ולעיתים אף עוינות גלויה. התשובה הנכונה שומרת על "doubt, and at times even open hostility".

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The two outcomes are ____ different despite identical starting points.
questions.e: Strikingly = באופן בולט. נקודות פתיחה זהות מדגישות הבדל בולט.

questions.p: The technology is ____ in theory but rarely used in practice.
questions.e: הניגוד "in theory but rarely in practice" מחייב מילה חיובית: available (זמינה).

questions.p: The data were ____, pointing in two opposite directions at once.
questions.e: Equivocal = דו-משמעי. נתונים המצביעים לשני כיוונים הם דו-משמעיים.

questions.p: The two explanations are not rivals but ____ accounts of one process.
questions.e: Complementary = משלימים. "not rivals but" מחייב יחס משלים בין ההסברים.

questions.p: The argument ____ under the weight of its own contradictions.
questions.e: Collapse = להתמוטט. סתירות פנימיות גורמות לטיעון להתמוטט.

questions.p: The evidence is ____ enough to justify further, but not final, study.
questions.e: Suggestive = מרמז/מעורר. ראיה שמצדיקה מחקר נוסף אך לא סופית היא מרמזת בלבד.

description: סימולציה מאתגרת בשישה פרקי הליבה של האמירנט, ברמה גבוהה ומיועדת למי שמכוון לציון גבוה.

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The findings were ____ across different countries and cultures.
questions.e: Replicate = לשחזר. הממצאים שוחזרו במדינות ובתרבויות שונות.

questions.p: The plan looked promising but ____ under closer scrutiny.
questions.e: Collapse = להתמוטט. "promising but ... under scrutiny" מחייב פועל המציין כישלון.

questions.p: The institution has a ____ reputation built over many decades.
questions.e: Distinguished = נכבד/מכובד. מוניטין שנבנה לאורך עשורים הוא מכובד.

questions.p: The study’s conclusions are ____ to the assumptions built into its model.
questions.e: Sensitive to = רגיש ל. המסקנות רגישות להנחות שבבסיס המודל.

questions.p: The text ____ a tension that the author never fully resolves.
questions.e: Embody = לגלם/להכיל בתוכו. הטקסט מגלם מתח שאינו נפתר.

questions.p: The lecture was ____ with insight, repaying the listener’s full attention.
questions.e: Replete with = רווי/מלא ב. הרצאה רוויה בתובנות מתגמלת קשב מלא.

sections.descHe: בכל שאלה מופיע משפט באנגלית עם מילה חסרה. בחרו מתוך ארבע אפשרויות את המילה או הביטוי שמשלימים את המשפט בצורה הטובה ביותר, לפי אוצר המילים, הדקדוק ורמזי ההקשר.

questions.p: The policy had a ____ effect, helping some while harming others.
questions.e: Mixed = מעורב. עזרה לחלק ופגיעה באחרים מצביעה על השפעה מעורבת.

questions.p: The two factors are ____, making it hard to study them separately.
questions.e: Intertwined = שזורים זה בזה. אם קשה להפרידם, הם שזורים.

questions.p: The author writes with a ____ that few of her peers can match.
questions.e: Fluency = שטף. כתיבה שמעטים משתווים לה מצטיינת בשטף.

questions.p: His argument ____ a question that has puzzled scholars for centuries.
questions.e: Revive = להחיות/לעורר מחדש. הטיעון מעורר מחדש שאלה עתיקה.

questions.p: The reasoning is ____, drawing a universal rule from a single case.
questions.e: Overgeneralized = מוכלל יתר על המידה. גזירת כלל אוניברסלי ממקרה יחיד היא הכללת יתר.

questions.p: The hypothesis is elegant ____ ultimately untestable.
questions.e: יש ניגוד בין האלגנטיות לבין חוסר היכולת לבחון, ולכן but.

questions.p: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Infrastructure only matters when new projects are built.
Infrastructure has no effect on people’s lives.
Infrastructure is mostly invisible yet quietly shapes society and opportunity.
Visible projects are always more useful than infrastructure.
questions.e: הרעיון המרכזי: התשתית בלתי נראית ברובה אך מעצבת בשקט את החברה ואת ההזדמנויות.

questions.p: When does infrastructure tend to attract attention?
o: When no one depends on it.
questions.e: נכתב: "Infrastructure ... tends to attract attention only when it fails".

questions.p: Why is the invisibility of infrastructure described as a measure of success?
o: Well-designed infrastructure works unnoticed in the background.
Invisible infrastructure does no work at all.
Success requires infrastructure to fail often.

passages.title: Translation as Interpretation
passages.text: It is tempting to imagine translation as a mechanical task: replace each word in one language with its equivalent in another, and the meaning will carry across intact. Anyone who has attempted serious translation knows how misleading this picture is. Words rarely map neatly onto one another, and a single term may carry connotations, rhythms, and cultural associations that have no exact counterpart elsewhere. The translator must therefore make continual judgments, deciding what to preserve and what, regrettably, to sacrifice. A version that captures the literal sense may lose the tone; one that preserves the music may stray from the precise meaning. Far from being a neutral conduit, the translator is an interpreter whose choices shape how a text is understood. This is why two skilled translators, working from the same original, can produce strikingly different results, each defensible in its own terms. Translation, properly understood, is less a transfer than a creative act of interpretation.

questions.p: What is the central claim of the passage?
o: Translation is a simple word-for-word replacement.
Translation is an interpretive, creative act rather than a mechanical transfer.
Good translation requires no judgment at all.
Only one correct translation can ever exist.
questions.e: הטענה המרכזית: התרגום הוא מעשה פרשני ויצירתי ולא העברה מכנית.

That every language has the same words.
questions.e: נכתב: "replace each word in one language with its equivalent in another, and the meaning will carry across intact".

questions.p: Why do words rarely map neatly onto one another?
o: All languages use the exact same grammar.
Words never have more than one meaning.

Translators refuse to look up words.
questions.e: נכתב: "a single term may carry connotations, rhythms, and cultural associations that have no exact counterpart elsewhere".

questions.p: What trade-off does the passage describe?
o: A translation can always keep both perfectly.
Tone and meaning are exactly the same thing.

questions.e: נכתב: "A version that captures the literal sense may lose the tone; one that preserves the music may stray from the precise meaning".

questions.p: How does the passage describe the translator?

As a neutral conduit with no influence.
As a machine that follows fixed rules.
As someone who ignores the original text.
questions.e: נכתב: "Far from being a neutral conduit, the translator is an interpreter whose choices shape how a text is understood".
